items.headline: China finally gets its crown — Bilibili Gaming win Worlds, beating Gen.G
items.body: The League of Legends World Championship ended Saturday in Brooklyn with Bilibili Gaming toppling Gen.G 3-1 to lift their first-ever Summoner's Cup. It's China's first world title since 2021 and the end of a long run of Korean dominance — BLG beat all four Korean teams on the way to the trophy.
items.say: That League of Legends world final finally wrapped — a Chinese team, BLG, won it for the first time ever. Ended years of Korea running the show. You dip into any esports?

items.headline: Harrison shocks Nunes and Gane survives a war at the Garden
items.body: A wild night at Madison Square Garden: Kayla Harrison submitted the returning legend Amanda Nunes with a fourth-round rear-naked choke to keep her bantamweight belt, and in the main event Ciryl Gane outlasted unbeaten Josh Hokit over five rounds — landing a UFC heavyweight-record 237 significant strikes — to retain the title by unanimous decision.
items.say: Big UFC night at the Garden — Kayla Harrison actually submitted Amanda Nunes, and the heavyweight main event went the full five rounds. You catch any of the fights?

items.headline: Arch Manning's walk-off TD — Texas stuns LSU 22-21 with 3 seconds left
items.body: Down most of the second half in a hostile Baton Rouge, Texas marched down the field and Arch Manning hit Raleek Brown for a 4-yard touchdown with three seconds on the clock to win 22-21. A brutal, playoff-shaking night in the SEC that came down to the final snap.
items.say: Did you see the Texas–LSU finish? Arch Manning threw the game-winner with three seconds left in Baton Rouge — absolute heartbreak for LSU. You follow the college playoff race?

links.text: Manning's game-winning TD to Raleek Brown (SEC)

items.headline: Pulisic bags a brace as the USMNT batter Haiti 6-0
items.body: The U.S. men turned their Nations League quarterfinal first leg into a rout, thumping Haiti 6-0 with Christian Pulisic scoring twice and Auston Trusty, Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun all getting on the board. They head to Cincinnati on Tuesday for the second leg with the tie all but wrapped up.
items.say: The U.S. men put six past Haiti — Pulisic had two. They're cruising in that Nations League tie. You keeping an eye on the national team with the World Cup coming up?

items.headline: Tennis's season finale is underway in Turin — Zverev opens with a win
items.body: The year's top eight men are battling it out at the Nitto ATP Finals in Turin. Alexander Zverev got things rolling Sunday by handling teenage debutant Rafael Jodar in straight sets, and world No. 1 Carlos Alcaraz — riding a long win streak with Jannik Sinner hurt — makes his tournament debut Monday.
items.say: The ATP Finals are on in Turin this week — Alcaraz is the big favorite now that Sinner's out injured. You catch any tennis this time of year?

links.text: Zverev, Shelton, Fils & Jodar press conference (Tennis TV)

items.headline: The wait is almost over — 'GTA VI' finally launches Thursday
items.body: After years of hype and a string of delays, Grand Theft Auto VI lands November 19 on PS5 and Xbox — arguably the most anticipated entertainment release of the decade. It's set in a modern, neon-soaked Vice City with dual leads Jason and Lucia, and preloads are already live.
items.say: GTA 6 actually comes out Thursday — people have been waiting on this one for years. Might be the biggest launch ever. You planning to play it, or know someone who's counting down?

items.headline: Oasis, Phil Collins & Wu-Tang headline the 2026 Rock Hall class
items.body: The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inducted its 2026 class Saturday night in Los Angeles — a stacked list including Oasis, Phil Collins, Wu-Tang Clan, Sade, Billy Idol, Luther Vandross, Iron Maiden and Joy Division/New Order. U2 opened the show, with Queen Latifah and Celia Cruz among the early-influence honorees.
items.say: The Rock Hall just inducted its new class — Oasis, Phil Collins, Wu-Tang, Sade, all in. Pretty wild mix of eras. Who would be a no-brainer induction in your book?

items.headline: A country song just rewrote the record book — Ella Langley's historic No. 1
items.body: Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' has now spent a record-shattering run of more than 25 weeks atop the Billboard Hot 100 — the longest reign in the chart's entire history, passing even Mariah Carey's holiday juggernaut. A country breakout turning into one of the biggest chart stories ever.
items.say: There's a country song that's basically been No. 1 for half a year — Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' broke the all-time record. Have you heard it yet, or are you sick of it by now?

items.headline: An Oscar at last — Glenn Close & Ridley Scott honored tonight
items.body: Hollywood toasts two long-overdue legends at tonight's Governors Awards: Glenn Close, who holds the record for most acting nominations without a win (eight), and 'Gladiator' director Ridley Scott both receive honorary Oscars. Animator Floyd Norman is also honored.
items.say: Glenn Close is finally getting an Oscar tonight — an honorary one, after eight nominations and no wins. Kind of a feel-good moment. You have a favorite Glenn Close or Ridley Scott movie?
